steps.say: Mass is how heavy something is. We use grams (g) and kilograms (kg).
To read scales, first find what each mark is worth.

figure.alt: Scales from 0 to 1,000 g marked every 100 g. The pointer is at 600 g.

steps.say: Capacity is how much a container holds. We use millilitres (ml) and litres (l).
This jug is marked every 250 ml. The water is at 750 ml.

figure.alt: A jug marked every 250 ml up to 1,000 ml. The water is at 750 ml.

check.prompt: How much water is in the jug?
hints: Find what each mark on the jug is worth.
Count up the marks from the bottom.
Read the mark at the top of the water.
check.explanation: The marks go up in 100 ml. The water reaches 300 ml.

figure.alt: A jug marked every 100 ml up to 500 ml. The water is at 300 ml.

options.why: 1,500 g is 1 kg 500 g, which is less than 2 kg.

check.explanation: 2 kg = 2,000 g. That is more than 1,500 g, 1,000 g and 900 g.
